## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet. The starting architecture scored 0.000 on both seeds, so we can't measure seed noise from it. The default recipe gives only 32 PPO updates of 4096 samples, which may be too few for exact multi-brick builds. A placement is correct only if every footprint cell is missing at the layer where the brick lands, and that layer is the highest point under the whole footprint. The starting network squeezes each column into 32 numbers and then pools them, so working out which layer a brick lands on, and whether the target fills that layer, is hard for it. This round tests two things. First, whether fewer PPO epochs and more, smaller updates help the starting network on their own. Second, a per-layer network whose placement head scores each candidate landing layer and learns a soft gate over them, tried with 2 and with 1 PPO epochs.

### Round 2
All three trials scored 0 on dev for both seeds, and their train success was also 0. So the problem is that the agent learns nothing useful, not that it overfits. Two very different networks (the base 2D network and the per-layer network) and three recipes (4, 2 or 1 PPO epochs, 131k to 233k steps) gave identical results, so neither the amount of data nor the per-layer prior was the bottleneck. One likely cause is collapse early in training. Random placements mostly fill cells outside the target, so their reward is negative, while DONE pays 0. PPO may then learn to end episodes early and lose its entropy before it ever sees an exact build. A second possibility is that the world differs from the description, for example in its anchor or footprint convention, so the fixed footprint-pooling head looks at the wrong cells. This round tests a higher entropy bonus on its own, then a network with a slowed DONE head plus a learned 3x3 head that does not assume an anchor convention, then global attention.

### Round 3
All 6 trials scored exactly 0 on dev, and also 0 on training episodes late in training. They varied size, step count (131k to 266k), entropy, epochs, attention and a per-layer net, so the blocker is structural, not noise or capacity. Likely cause: an exact build needs DONE at exactly the right step, because any later placement adds extra cells. DONE is 1 logit against about 250 placement logits, so it starts near 1/250 probability. The +1 bonus is almost never seen, and r2c2's slowed DONE made this worse. Proposed fix: split the decision in two. A learned sigmoid gate chooses DONE or place (about 50% at start), then a softmax picks the placement. Candidate A adds only this to r1c1. B also uses 1 epoch for about 400k steps. C uses the deeper trunk plus a learned per-type 3x3 head, in case the anchor convention differs from the description. If all three stay at 0, DONE timing is ruled out.

### Round 4
All 9 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and on train success. Neither network type nor recipe made any difference: per-layer gating, attention, a deeper trunk, a learned 3x3 anchor head, entropy, DONE parameterisation, and 1 to 2 epochs with 230k to 405k steps all failed. Seed noise cannot explain a uniform zero. Some of these nets, such as the per-layer landing gate, should represent correct placements easily. That points to an assumption every net shares. Every head ties the action logit at (t, y, x) to obs features at the same (y, x). If this world decodes actions in a different spatial order (transposed, flipped or offset), no aligned convolutional head can learn it. The task warns that the world may differ from its description. So this round tests a learned position-remapping path into action space. It also feeds in the mask laid out in action coordinates, which shows the true action layout at the grid borders.
